title: Close a wall belt barrier: draw the belt, pass its end hand to hand against the spring, and lower it into the wall clip
instruction: Close the belt barrier: pull the belt out, lift its end over the wall clip and lower it down into the clip's slot.
context: Station, mall and airport staff close retractable belt barriers across escalators, aisles and queues daily. The belt of a wall unit is pulled out by its end, against the retractor, and the end hung on a clip on the facing wall: its fitting is lifted over the clip and lowered down into the clip's slot, whose lips hold it against the pull. If the belt slips from the hand, the retractor takes it back; an end pushed at the clip from the side, or held above it, does not go in. Working from one spot, as a fixed robot does, the belt changes hands mid-pull: the unit and the clip are 90 cm apart, each beyond the reach of the arm nearer the other. The webbing pulls 8.9 N throughout, so the second hand must take the belt just behind its 17 x 58 mm end before the first lets go, then lift the end 54 mm, square its 6 mm bead to an 8 mm channel and lower it 54 mm to the clip's foot. Unlike a loose cable passed between hands, the belt is under pull the whole way and its end must finish seated.
setup: Station: two YAM arms with parallel grippers at the near edge of the table. Wall: a 1220 x 610 mm (4 x 2 ft) sheet of 18 mm plywood standing on the table, its face along x = 45 cm. Tensabarrier 896-type wall unit: yellow case 100 mm deep, 115 mm long, 70 mm tall, 2 in (50 mm) belt, 13 ft, screwed to a 40 mm timber batten on the board; the belt leaves it through a slot in its mouth, and the end fitting, larger than the slot, stops against the mouth. Belt: woven polyester webbing 50 mm wide, 1.5 mm thick, 40 g/m. Belt end: a metal end fitting 17 mm long, 58 mm tall, 14 mm thick, 50 g; on its front face a neck 2.5 mm thick and 4.5 mm long and behind it a bead 6 mm across and 3.5 mm long, both 28 mm tall, centred on the end's height. Wall receiver: a Tensabarrier 898 wall clip, black metal, 112 mm tall, 16 mm wide along the belt and 11 mm deep, its two 4 mm screw holes 90 mm apart (the maker's drawing), screwed to a stand-off of three 2x4 offcuts (38 x 89 mm, 130 mm long) screwed face to face, 114 mm deep, so that its face sits on the belt's line. The clip's slot runs top to bottom, opening toward the unit: two lips 3 mm thick with a 4 mm gap between them, and behind them a channel 8 mm across and 5 mm deep, closed at the bottom by the clip's 11 mm foot and 50 mm tall; the lips' top inner edges are chamfered 1 mm. Above the channel the lips are cut away for 36 mm (the entry window), under a 15 mm head that carries the top screw. The bead goes in through the window, over the channel, and is lowered down it: the neck runs in the gap, the bead behind the lips, which it overlaps by 1 mm on each side, until the bead stands on the foot. There is no latch: the lips hold the bead against the belt's pull, and its weight keeps it down (metal on metal friction 0.25). The maker publishes the clip's outline and screw spacing; the slot's sizes and the end fitting are our estimates, read from the drawing and the photograph of the end, and are measured on the real parts (Building it). Layout in the line frame (cm, table top z = 0; x forward from the arm bases, y to the robot's left): arm bases at y = -30.5 and +30.5; the belt runs along the wall in the plane x = 33, its centre at z = 13; the unit's mouth is at y = -44 and the clip's face toward it at y = +46, 90 cm apart, 17 and 15 cm from the board's ends; the clip's foot is 10.5 cm above the table. The belt is a chain of 37 rigid links 25 mm long, each hinged to the next, in turn about the belt's width (it bends flat round what it meets, stiffness 0.004 N m2) and about its thickness (edgewise, 0.25 N m2); it sags under its weight and cannot stretch; twist is not modelled: the belt cannot twist about its length, a shortcut (a real webbing twists and the end fitting can turn on it; here the end is squared by the hand's pose alone). The end fitting is its last link, held by nothing but the belt, the hands, the unit's mouth and the clip. Inside the unit the belt runs back to the reel, which pulls it in with 8.9 N, constant: the pull of a 2 lb (8.9 N) constant-force spring. The maker publishes no retractor force; we estimate 5 to 12 N for a unit of this size. A lab checks the pull with a 1 kg spring scale on the end at 0.1, 0.5 and 0.86 m out, and uses the unit as sold if it reads 7 to 11 N (the range the demo was run at), or else fits that spring (8.9 N within 0.5 N). The retractor's brake is modelled as damping of the reel's travel, 7.2 N s/m, so a released end runs back at about 1.2 m/s. Both grippers start at the arms' ready pose. Start state, the same every trial: the belt fully in, the end against the unit's mouth.
scoring: Terms: seated means the end's bead is down the wall clip's channel, behind its lips, both its top and bottom within the channel, and its bottom within 3 mm of the clip's foot, so it was lowered at least 47 of the channel's 50 mm (real trial: the end's top edge at the mark on the board, by video). Belt out is the length of belt drawn out of the unit's mouth (real trial: tape on the wall every 10 cm). A hand holds when its jaws are shut on the end or on the belt within 20 cm of it. Straight means the belt drawn out has no fold or snag: nowhere is it bent flat more than 30 degrees (a taut run bends under 5; real trial: video). Clear means no fingertip, gripper body or palm of either hand within 5 cm of the end's centre lines (along its length and its height) or of the last 20 cm of belt (its middle line and both edges), and no hand shut on the belt anywhere along it; still means the end's centre moves under 1 mm in that second (real trial: video). The tiers are read at the last step, the 1.0 over the last 1 s; a run-back of the belt on the way costs nothing by itself. Four steps, one tier each. 0.2: the belt drawn out, belt out at least 0.5 m with a hand holding. 0.4: handed over, that, with the left hand the one holding. 0.6: seated in the clip. 1.0: left to the clip, seated and clear and still for the last 1 s, held by the clip and its own weight alone, belt out at least 0.5 m. One failure voids the run: the belt folded or snagged at the end (not straight) scores 0. 0 otherwise. Possible scores: 0, 0.2, 0.4, 0.6, 1.0.
fidelity: Belt: 37 rigid links 25x50x1.5 mm, 40 g/m, hinged flatwise (EI 0.004 N m2, est. 0.001-0.01) and edgewise (0.25, est. 0.1-1); no stretch. Belt twist is not modelled (hinges only flatwise/edgewise), so it cannot cause failure. Reel: 8.9 N constant pull (2 lb spring; real est. 5-12 N), brake 7.2 N s/m. End fitting 17x58x14 mm, 50 g (thickness, mass est.). Clip: Tensabarrier 898 outline; slot, bead est. No latch: lips and gravity hold the end. Demo reads the end's pose.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0; demo: 1.0. Lazy routes: none, right hand alone, let go, pushed at face, flat pinch 0; handed over and carried on, held over slot, lowered short, end under clip 0.4; hand shut behind seated end 0.4-0.6.
reset_notes: Nothing is random (object_jitter=0). Between real trials let the belt run fully back, the end against the unit's mouth.
